title: First Determination of the Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation Temperature at z = 0.68 Using Molecular Absorption Lines
question: What is the cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation temperature at z = 0.68 derived from rotational molecular absorption lines toward the lensed quasar B0218+357, and is it consistent with the standard Big Bang cosmological model?

evidence.quote: The cosmic microwave background (CMB; (cite: Penzias_1965; Dicke_1965)) is a nearly uniform, isotropic blackbody radiation field with a current temperature of $2.72548\pm0.00057\,\mathrm{K}$ (cite: Fixsen_2009).

what.value: Hydrogen column densities N(H I) = 5e20 cm^-2, N(H2) = (0.1-2)e22 cm^-2, kinetic temperature T_kin = 55 K, and gas density n(H2) ~ 10^(2-4) cm^-3 (and 5e3 cm^-3 for RADEX)

evidence.quote: Assuming that $N_\mathrm{H}$ toward the $z\!=\!0.68$ absorber is given by the sum of $N$($\mathrm{H}\,$I) $\!=\!5\times10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ and $N({\rm H}_2)\!=$(0.1–2)$\times10^{22}\,{\rm cm}^{-2}$, as estimated by (cite: Henkel_2005)

we performed RADEX (cite: vanderTak_2007) calculations adopting the physical conditions of the $z\!=\!0.68$ absorbing cloud ($T_\mathrm{kin}\!=\!55 \,\mathrm{K}$ and $n(\mathrm{H_2})\!=\!5\times10^3\, \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$) reported by (cite: Henkel_2005).

what.value: Continuum covering factor lower limit f_c >= 0.77 for component A

evidence.quote: For the A component, (cite: Muller_2007) estimated $f_\mathrm{c}\geq0.77$ from the saturated absorption bottom of the $\sim5\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ component of the HCO$^+$ $J$=2–1 line.

what.value: Lognormal N-PDF parameters for Orion A giant molecular cloud used for nonuniformity optical depth correction

evidence.quote: In this study, we adopted the N-PDF parameters derived by (cite: Ma_2020) for the Orion A giant molecular cloud, which has a comparable mean column density of $\sim 1.5\times10^{22}\,{\rm cm}^{-2}$ (cite: Ma_2020), to compute the correction.

what.value: Initial column densities for HCN (7.8e13 cm^-2) and HCO+ (4.5e13 cm^-2), and line widths for RADEX (17, 17, 10 km/s for HCN, HCO+, HNC)

evidence.quote: For the initial column densities, we adopted $7.8\times10^{13}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ and $4.5\times10^{13}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ for HCN and HCO$^{+}$, respectively, as reported by (cite: WiklindCombes_1995).

The line widths were set to approximately 17 $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, 17 $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, and 10 $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ for HCN, HCO$^{+}$, and HNC, respectively, based on the spectra reported in (cite: WiklindCombes_1995).

what.value: Abundance ratio N(HNC)/N(HCN) measured in the PKS1830-211 absorber used to estimate initial HNC column density

evidence.quote: we estimated the initial value using the abundance ratio $N(\mathrm{HNC})/N(\mathrm{HCN})$ measured in the PKS1830–211 absorber (cite: Muller_2011; Muller_2016)

what.value: Initial column densities (2.9e12 cm^-2 for H13CN, 2.0e12 cm^-2 for H13CO+) and RADEX line widths (6.3 km/s and 4.5 km/s) for 13C isotopologues

evidence.quote: The initial values of $N$ were adopted from (cite: Wallstrom_2016), namely $2.9\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ for H$^{13}$CN and $2.0\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ for H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$.
together with line widths of approximately 6.3 $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and 4.5 $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ for H$^{13}$CN and H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$, respectively (cite: Wallstrom_2016).

what.value: Compilation of approximately 80 previous measurements of T_CMB(z) from the literature

evidence.quote: In addition to the new measurement of $T_\mathrm{CMB}$ at $z\!=\!0.68$ obtained in this work, the figure includes approximately 80 previous measurements in the literature (cite: Battistelli_2002; Luzzi_2009; Muller_2013; Klimenko_2020; Riechers_2022; Kotani_2025).

external_data.citation: (cite: Battistelli_2002; Luzzi_2009; Muller_2013; Klimenko_2020; Riechers_2022; Kotani_2025)

recipe.goal: Extractspectral windows and regrid velocity axis
recipe.method: Extract spectral windows containing target absorption lines and regrid spectral axis to minimum velocity resolution in barycentric frame using relativistic Doppler conversion
key_parameters: bandwidths: 0.23 GHz (0.47 GHz for Band 4 HNC) for HCN, HCO+, HNC; 0.12 GHz (Band 3) and 0.94 GHz (Band 4) for H13CN and H13CO+

recipe.goal: Extract absorption spectra toward lensed quasar component A
recipe.method: Direct visibility fitting in the Fourier plane using a two-point-source model: (1) determine peak positions from continuum visibilities, (2) fit visibilities in each spectral channel at fixed positions
assumptions: Two compact lensed components can be modeled as two point sources; no significant time variability over the 9-month observation interval

recipe.goal: Compute optical depth profiles and propagate covering factor uncertainties
recipe.method: Monte Carlo sampling of continuum covering factor f_c and continuum-normalized absorption depth to compute optical depth probability distribution, followed by correction for lognormal column-density nonuniformity
assumptions: Lognormal column density distribution with parameters from Orion A GMC (mean N(H2) ~ 1.5e22 cm^-2)

recipe.goal: Derive excitation temperatures T_ex from J=2-1 and J=3-2 optical depths
recipe.method: Resample HCN, HCO+, HNC spectra to ΔV_bar = 0.909 km/s and fit Boltzmann optical depth relation (Eq. 3) per velocity bin where tau < 1, then take weighted mean over +5 km/s component; for H13CN and H13CO+, fit single Gaussian to optical depth, integrate over [-5, +15] km/s, and fit Eq. 3
key_parameters: ΔV_bar = 0.909 km/s; tau < 1 cutoff; initial T_ex = 4.59 K; initial N = 7.8e13, 4.5e13, 2.6e13, 2.9e12, 2.0e12 cm^-2 for HCN, HCO+, HNC, H13CN, H13CO+
assumptions: Rotational levels follow a Boltzmann distribution characterized by a single excitation temperature T_ex

recipe.goal: Determine T_CMB(z=0.68) and constrain cosmological deviation parameter beta
recipe.method: Compute weighted mean of HCN and HNC excitation temperatures assuming T_CMB = T_ex, and fit Lima et al. (2000) scaling relation T_CMB(z) = T_0(1+z)^(1-beta) to combined literature compilation
assumptions: Radiative equilibrium with the CMB (T_CMB = T_ex), negligible local dust emission and negligible collisional excitation for HCN and HNC in optically thin regime

evidence.quote: From a weighted mean of the excitation temperatures obtained from HCN and HNC, we determined the CMB temperature at $z\!=\!0.68$ to be ${4.50\pm0.17\,\mathrm{K}}$.

answer_key.quantity: Peak optical depth of H13CN and H13CO+ J=3-2 lines

evidence.quote: In contrast, the H$^{13}$CN and H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ lines are optically thin in both transitions, with $\tau_{\rm max}\!\sim\!0.10$–0.15 for the *J*=2–1 lines and $\tau_{\rm max}\!\sim\!0.04$–0.05 for the *J*=3–2 lines.

answer_key.quantity: Continuum covering factor lower limit from HCN J=2-1 saturation

evidence.quote: If we assume that the optical depth becomes infinite at the absorption minimum, Equation (\[eq:taudef\]) yields a lower limit of $f_{\rm c} \sim 0.8$, which is consistent with the constraint $f_{\rm c} \ge 0.77$.

score_reason: Archival ALMA data are publicly available, calibrators and spectral window widths are explicitly given, and the visibility fitting (UVMULTIFIT) and statistical steps (Monte Carlo f_c sampling, tau < 1 filtering, velocity ranges, initial fit values, and bin counts in Table 1) are well documented. Reproduction only requires consulting Kotani et al. (2025) for the exact lognormal N-PDF correction curve and standard molecular spectroscopic databases for Einstein A coefficients.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival dataset (2016.1.00031.S) with a clean, quantitative target outcome (T_ex per species in Table 1 and final T_CMB(z=0.68) = 4.50 +/- 0.17 K) and a well-specified visibility-fitting + Monte Carlo analytical pipeline.
